title: BH-Exit: Label-Free Early Termination for HNSW Search via Bucket-Histogram Stability

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to enable label-free early termination of HNSW search by detecting convergence earlier than exact ID matching. This is a specific objective within the broader area of approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search. Paper [3] discusses "Learned Adaptive Early Termination" for ANN search, which also aims to terminate search early, but it relies on learned models rather than label-free convergence detection. Paper [6] introduces a "Simple Early Termination Strategy for HNSW Graph Traversal," which is directly relevant as it also focuses on early termination in HNSW search. While the specific method differs, the purpose of enabling early termination in HNSW search is shared. Therefore, the purpose is covered by [6].

### Mechanism
The mechanism, BH-Exit, monitors bucket-histogram stability by assigning corpus vectors to buckets via offline k-means clustering and terminating search when the L1 distance between consecutive bucket histograms falls below a threshold. Paper [8] discusses histogram testing and L1 distance measures for distinguishing distributions, which aligns with the histogram-based stability monitoring in BH-Exit. Paper [13] introduces the "Annular Bucket Histogram" for spatial selectivity estimation, which also involves bucket-based histogram representations, though in a different context. However, neither [8] nor [13] applies these histogram techniques to early termination in ANN search. Paper [6] uses a different mechanism for early termination in HNSW, not involving histograms or bucket stability. Thus, the specific mechanism of BH-Exit appears to be novel.

### Evaluation
The evaluation involves coarse-grained monitoring that ignores within-bucket churn, enabling earlier convergence detection than ID-Overlap. Paper [6] evaluates early termination strategies for HNSW search, which aligns with the evaluation design of comparing termination strategies in HNSW. While the specific metrics or benchmarks may differ, the evaluation design of comparing early termination effectiveness in HNSW search is shared. Therefore, the evaluation is covered by [6].

### Domain
The domain is approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) / HNSW dense retrieval search. Papers [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], and [7] all operate in the domain of ANN search, with several specifically addressing HNSW-based methods. Since the contribution operates within this well-established domain, the domain is covered.
